action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Untapped capability: proposed Encore (encore-widget), Pen (pen-widget), Wire (wire-widget)
Person at the terminal: proposed Customs (customs-widget), Gear (gear-widget)
Delight: proposed Blink (blink-widget), Later (later-widget), Colophon (colophon-widget)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Encore": Not chosen: the API allows it, but a verbatim replay only fits rituals with no changing arguments (a version bump or commit message replays yesterday's values), and ok-or-failed divergence cannot see a step that succeeds with stale input, so the risk outweighs what a shell script already gives.

stamped reject on "Pen": Not chosen: reading the streamed arguments is new beside stream-widget and diff-widget, but the gain is a few seconds of early warning on a call the permission dialog and diff already cover.

stamped reject on "Wire": A variation on watch-widget joined to situation-widget's prompt context, and it only works if you move your dev server out of your own terminal into a no-shell child the widget owns.

stamped reject on "Gear": Cost out of proportion: a keyword rule silently lowers how hard the model thinks, the wrong guess is a poorer answer you may not notice, and the claimed saving cannot be measured against the turn that did not run.
stamped reject on "Blink": Not chosen: a pleasant mirror, but it is guard-widget's ask count with a stopwatch and an invented reading time, and it changes nothing a person does.

stamped reject on "Later": A variation on owed-widget, parking-widget and lessons-widget built on premise-widget's phrase matcher, and phrase matching on 'later' and 'for now' will quote mostly noise.
stamped reject on "Colophon": Cost out of proportion: it writes turn counts, corrections and the hour permanently into a shared git history for a novelty line few teams would accept.
named the widget customs-widget ("Customs")

stamped pass: Customs is the only idea that brings a fact from outside the machine to the moment of decision: it checks each package Claude names against the real registry and holds installs of missing or days-old names, with no model call, on API that exists.

stamped pass: Built customs-widget: a tool.check gate on Bash and PowerShell that looks each installed npm or PyPI name up before the command runs, lists the findings on the card and raises an allow to an ask for a missing or under-30-day name, with show, trust and clear and 15 acceptance tests.

live run made, a good run: the install of a name not on npm was held by the widget's own ask with the gate line as its reason and the headless host refused it, show listed that name as held and is-odd as on npm 11 years, 1M downloads last week, latest 3.0.1, the store holds isOn false; npm is not on this machine's Bash PATH, so the dry run itself failed with command not found after its package was checked
